facts.material: woven 100% polyamide (hood, sleeves, back yoke, shoulders) and knit 82% polyester/18% elastane (balance); all man-made fibers
facts.function: outerwear jacket (anorak/windbreaker type) with hood and full zipper front
facts.form: complete garment, removable hood and sleeves, neither fabric over 60% of visible surface

gri_path: GRI 1: the jacket is prima facie classifiable in 6101 (knit) and 6201 (woven) because it combines knit and woven components; chapter 61 and 62 notes do not resolve it
GRI 3(a): each heading refers to only part of the materials, so they are equally specific
GRI 3(b): per the facts, neither the knit nor the woven fabric imparts the essential character
GRI 3(c): heading 6201 (woven) occurs last in numerical order over 6101

GRI 6: 6201.40 of man-made fibers; anoraks, windbreakers and similar; not recreational performance outerwear (no waterproof/taped-seam facts), no down, not water resistant stated; Other: Men's (634), 6201.40.75.11

rejected_alternatives.reason: knit heading; under GRI 3(c) the later heading 6201 prevails when neither fabric gives essential character
water resistant line; no water resistance (AATCC 35) stated
recreational performance outerwear requires specific features (waterproof, taped seams etc.) not described
suit-type jacket/blazer; this is a hooded zip-front outerwear jacket

classification.rationale: The jacket has knit and woven components, neither exceeding 60 percent of visible surface and neither giving essential character, so GRI 3(b) fails and GRI 3(c) sends it to 6201, the later of 6101 and 6201. It is an anorak/windbreaker-type jacket of man-made fibers (polyamide and polyester). NY N353235 classified a men's knit/woven outer jacket of man-made fibers in 6201.40.7511, the same statistical line used here, absent water-resistance or performance-outerwear features.
